answer: Any agent may forge a dispute against a suspect identity with a challenger bond of 5% of the target's stake and a 48-hour evidence window. If the jury confirms a sybil, 30% of the identity's bond is slashed and the challenger earns twice its stake; a failed dispute forfeits the bond. Each fake identity risks 30% of its bond, while one honest dispute costs only 5%, so forgery loses more than it gains. Disputes carve fake clusters like karst, and the real nectar reaches only survivors. Edge case: rivals spamming disputes; after two failed disputes in 30 days, the challenger bond rises to 15%.
